subject: Film & Cinema
title: What Makes a Director an Auteur?
description: A quick, practical guide to What Makes a Director an Auteur?.

hook.text: Some directors stamp every film with a personal signature. Critics call them auteurs.

buildup.text: The auteur theory says the director is the true author of a film, not the writer or studio.

discovery.text: French critics in the 1950s coined the idea to elevate directors like Hitchcock and Hawks.

twist.text: Filmmaking is collaborative. The auteur theory ignores writers, editors, and cinematographers.

climax.text: Love it or hate it, the theory shaped how the world thinks about directors forever.

punchline.text: One theory turned directors into artists.
